axisDefinitions.ten: A desired result controls the steps.
Updates produce new values and preserve old values.

axisDefinitions.zero: One local instance performs the work.
axisDefinitions.ten: Multiple network nodes coordinate the work.
Runtime commands can change system behavior.

axisDefinitions.zero: A managed interface hides machine details.
axisDefinitions.ten: The system defines or directly controls hardware.

axisDefinitions.zero: One general artifact serves many tasks.
axisDefinitions.ten: The build selects components for a specific task.
Durable state is a principal system function.

method: Manual estimates from the cited sources. Scores describe the stated scope, not code quality or measured performance.
uncertainty: A score of 5 can mark uncertain evidence, as its reason states. Review those scores before a substantive conclusion.
compatibility: These study axes do not replace user axes. Joint PCA requires paradigm scores on these exact axis definitions.

repos.name: SQLite
repos.scope: The database engine, not an application that embeds it.

reasons.reason: SQL describes queries rather than explicit file operations.
The database file holds mutable application data.
The source describes local storage for individual applications and devices.
Applications issue SQL queries during execution.
The engine exposes database files rather than hardware interfaces.
The documented uses span devices, desktop files, and websites.
The embedded engine shares its application process.
The database file is a principal output of the engine.

repos.name: Redis
repos.scope: The data structure server, with Redis Cluster available.

reasons.reason: The README describes commands for data structures as well as a query engine.
The README describes updates to lists, sets, and other data structures.
Redis Cluster distributes data across network nodes.
The README describes commands, expiration policies, and optional modules.
Clients use a server interface rather than hardware interfaces.
The README describes one server for caches, queues, and queries.
Cluster nodes provide separate failure boundaries, but large failures stop the cluster.
Redis offers snapshots and an append-only log, but also permits a cache with no persistence.

repos.name: Erlang/OTP
repos.scope: The Erlang runtime and its process model.

reasons.reason: Pattern matches select messages, while explicit functions control process behavior.
Processes exchange values without shared data.
The manual describes communication across distributed Erlang nodes.
Processes can start new processes during execution.
The runtime exposes processes and messages rather than hardware interfaces.
The README offers a runtime and reusable libraries for many applications.
Processes share no data and each process has its own message queue.
The process tutorial does not establish durability. The midpoint marks uncertain evidence.

repos.name: Unikraft
repos.scope: One Unikraft image and its internal libraries.

reasons.reason: The README describes component selection for a custom kernel.
The README does not establish an immutable state model. The midpoint marks uncertain evidence.
This profile covers one image and its local library services. Network access alone does not require coordination across nodes.
The README emphasizes custom kernel construction rather than runtime component changes.
The README describes kernels and platform-specific optimizations.
The README explicitly selects only necessary OS components.
The application and OS libraries share one address space, with no kernel and user separation.
The README does not establish a durable state model. The midpoint marks uncertain evidence.
Chisel describes hardware and the generator emits RTL for a configured SoC.
The generated core includes mutable registers and caches.
The README describes an on-chip TileLink bus rather than a network cluster.
The generator elaborates the hardware configuration before execution.
The generator emits RTL for cores, caches, buses, and peripheral devices.
Configurations select core and SoC components before RTL generation.
The README does not establish component failure boundaries. The midpoint marks uncertain evidence.
The README emphasizes cores and caches rather than a durable data store.

repos.name: Nix
repos.scope: The package manager and its package model.

reasons.reason: Nix expressions describe package dependencies and build tasks.
Package contents never change after the build.
Binary caches distribute artifacts, but do not establish distributed coordination. The midpoint marks uncertain evidence.
Profiles can change at runtime, while package contents remain fixed.
The package manager operates on packages and paths rather than hardware interfaces.
Expressions select dependencies and variants before a package build.
Separate store paths prevent one package upgrade from replacing another package dependency.
The store retains package versions and supports rollback.

repos.name: seL4
repos.scope: One seL4 kernel and the protection domains under its control, without higher-level file or network services.

reasons.reason: C and assembly implement the kernel mechanisms. User code supplies explicit system calls and resource policies.
System calls change capability tables, thread state, and address space maps in place.
The kernel controls local memory, interrupts, and processor time. Network services require higher-level code.
User code can create kernel objects and revoke capabilities after boot.
The privileged kernel directly controls physical address space, interrupts, and processor time.
The README identifies build tools and kernel options but does not establish task specialization. The midpoint marks uncertain evidence.
Capabilities restrict access across protection domains. User code must configure those domains and their rights.
Files require higher-level services. The kernel itself supplies memory and execution mechanisms rather than durable storage.

paradigmScope: Each profile describes one cited example of an existing seed. Scores do not describe every implementation of that paradigm.

paradigms.name: Ownership types
paradigms.definition: The compiler checks one owner per value and releases the value when its owner leaves scope.
paradigms.scope: Rust memory ownership rules, not the whole Rust language or a Rust application.

reasons.reason: The compiler checks ownership rules rather than explicit memory release commands.
Ownership permits mutable strings and does not preserve each old value.
The rules control local stack and heap memory, not coordination across nodes.
The compiler fixes ownership rules before execution, although allocation occurs at runtime.
The model exposes stack, heap, pointers, and explicit value lifetimes.
The chapter does not establish component selection at build time. The midpoint marks uncertain evidence.
Ownership prevents invalid memory access but does not establish separate process failure boundaries.
Values leave memory when their owners leave scope. Durable storage is outside this model.

paradigms.name: Pipelined RISC processor
paradigms.definition: A processor overlaps instruction stages to execute an instruction stream.
paradigms.scope: One generated Rocket core with its caches, not the whole Rocket Chip generator or a network of cores.

reasons.reason: The generated core executes a scalar instruction stream.
The core changes cache contents and branch prediction state.
This profile covers one core with local caches, not coordination across network nodes.
The generated pipeline fixes instruction execution mechanisms before runtime.
The profile describes processor hardware and cache structures directly.
Generator parameters select ISA extensions, pipeline stages, and cache sizes.
Privilege levels protect access but do not establish independent component failures. The midpoint marks uncertain evidence.
The described core emphasizes instruction execution and caches, not a durable data store.

paradigms.name: Unikernel
paradigms.definition: An application and its required OS libraries form one image with one address space.
paradigms.scope: One Unikraft image and its internal libraries.

reasons.reason: KConfig selects the libraries and options that form the image.
The concepts page does not establish an immutable state model. The midpoint marks uncertain evidence.
The profile covers one image. Cloud deployment does not itself require coordination across nodes.
The build combines the selected libraries into one executable image.
The image can directly control hardware on a hypervisor or bare metal.
The image includes only the OS components that its application requires.
The application and OS libraries share one address space with no kernel and user separation.
File system access is an optional library service. The midpoint marks uncertain durability requirements.

paradigms.name: Embedded database
paradigms.definition: A database engine executes inside its application process and accesses files without a separate server.
paradigms.scope: The SQLite engine as an embedded database example, not a distributed application that uses SQLite.

reasons.reason: SQL queries describe the requested data through the database interface.
Applications read and write the database file directly through the engine.
The engine requires no separate process or network service.
Applications issue database queries during execution.
The engine exposes data files through the host file system.
The same engine serves devices, application files, and websites.
The engine and application share an address space, so client faults can corrupt engine memory.
The engine maintains database files on disk.

paradigms.name: Hardware generators
paradigms.definition: A parameterized program composes hardware components and emits a circuit description for a selected configuration.
paradigms.scope: The generated Rocket Chip system, with the same scope as the repository profile.

reasons.reason: Chisel descriptions and configuration parameters determine the generated circuit.
The generated cores contain mutable registers and caches.
The generated system connects components through an on-chip bus.
Elaboration fixes the circuit before execution.
The output describes processor cores, caches, and interconnect hardware.
Configuration parameters select components before circuit generation.
The README does not establish separate component failure boundaries. The midpoint marks uncertain evidence.
The documented output emphasizes cores and caches rather than durable data storage.

paradigms.name: Actor model
paradigms.definition: Independent actors own their state and talk only through asynchronous messages.
paradigms.scope: The Erlang runtime and its process model, with the same scope as the repository profile. Other actor implementations can differ.

reasons.reason: Patterns select messages, while functions specify process actions.
Processes exchange values without shared data.
The tutorial sends messages between processes on separate computers.
Processes create new processes through spawn at runtime.
The interface exposes processes and messages rather than hardware details.
The tutorial reuses process functions across examples rather than task-specific circuit or kernel artifacts.
Each process has private data and its own message queue.
The tutorial does not establish durability. The midpoint marks uncertain evidence.

paradigms.name: Functional package management
paradigms.definition: Packages are immutable values with explicit dependencies, so new versions coexist without changes to old versions.
paradigms.scope: The Nix package manager and its package model, with the same scope as the repository profile.

reasons.reason: Nix expressions specify dependencies and package build tasks.
Package contents never change after the build.
Binary caches supply packages but do not establish coordination across nodes. The midpoint marks uncertain evidence.
Profiles select package versions at runtime while package contents stay fixed.
The package model exposes store paths and dependencies rather than hardware controls.
Expressions select package dependencies and variants before the build.
Separate store paths preserve dependencies across upgrades. This score concerns dependency isolation, not process faults.
The store preserves old package versions for rollback.

paradigms.name: Data structure server
paradigms.definition: A server stores native data structures and exposes commands that operate on their contents directly.
paradigms.scope: The data structure server, with Redis Cluster available.

reasons.reason: Commands operate directly on native data structures, although the server also supports queries.
Commands change the contents of lists, sets, hashes, and other stored values.
Redis Cluster divides the data across network nodes.
Runtime commands control data, expiration policies, and optional modules.
Clients use a server interface rather than direct hardware controls.
The same server supports caches, queues, and queries.
Separate nodes tolerate some failures, but larger failures make the cluster unavailable.
Snapshots and an append-only log can preserve data, but a cache can disable persistence.

paradigms.name: Capability-based OS
paradigms.definition: A process can use a resource only through an unforgeable capability that names it.
paradigms.scope: One seL4 kernel and the protection domains under its control, without higher-level file or network services.

reasons.reason: C and assembly implement the kernel mechanisms. User code supplies explicit system calls and resource policies.
System calls change capability tables, thread state, and address space maps in place.
The kernel controls local memory, interrupts, and processor time. Network services require higher-level code.
User code can create kernel objects and revoke capabilities after boot.
The privileged kernel directly controls physical address space, interrupts, and processor time.
The README identifies build tools and kernel options but does not establish task specialization. The midpoint marks uncertain evidence.
Capabilities restrict access across protection domains. User code must configure those domains and their rights.
Files require higher-level services. The kernel itself supplies memory and execution mechanisms rather than durable storage.
